title: Morning Star
author: Pierce Brown
review:
I was beginning to get a little burnt out on this series towards the end, there's probably more padding in this book than the other two books. Although the ending is really well done and some of the twists and betrayals are pretty great. This book always tries to be a little bit deeper than just a fun action romp, it's partially successful, but there's some descriptions and themes that pull me out of it a little bit since they're not executed quite as well as they could be.

I will probably pick up the follow up trilogy once that's completed, the world is interesting and there's enough fallout *cough* to deal with after the events of the finale that I will be curious to see how they're handled in the next set of books.

highlights.text: Man is no island. We need those who love us. We need those who hate us. We need others to tether us to life, to give us a reason to live, to feel. All I have is the darkness.
“I said it once. Now I’ll say it twice. If there’s two things in this world that can’t be killed, it’s the fungus under my sack and the Reaper of bloodydamn Mars. Haha!”
He’s good at three things. Whining, stabbing people in the back, and destroying fleets.”
The Sons of Ares are guerilla fighters. Saboteurs. Spies. But in this war, Lorn’s words haunt me. “How do sheep kill a lion? By drowning him in blood.”
“I always dreamed of a good death.” He shudders as he realizes again that he’s dying. “This does not seem good.”

“I will give Eo your love. I will make a house for you in the Vale of your fathers. It will be beside my own. Join me there when you die.” He grins. “But I am no builder. So take your time. We will wait.”
“What is pride without honor? What is honor without truth? Honor is not what you say. It is not what you read.” Romulus thumps his chest. “Honor is what you do.”
Everything is cracked, everything is stained except the fragile moments that hang crystalline in time and make life worth living.

Look what befalls those who rise against, they will say. Look how even these mighty beasts fall before Gold. Who else can stand against them? No one. Their grip will tighten. Their reign will strengthen.
